title: Microsoft Purview DLP: set policy tips and email notifications separately for SharePoint and OneDrive rules (GCC, GCC High, DoD)
summary: The roadmap facts, notification behaviour, licensing and PowerShell command are supported. The portal route reaches the documented notification control but omits intermediate steps, and the checklist names override and alert controls that have no table rows.

claims.claim: The change decouples policy tips and email notifications in Microsoft Purview DLP rules for SharePoint and OneDrive.
claims.quote: Data Loss Prevention - Decoupling of Policy tips and Email notifications while configuring rules on Data Loss Prevention for Sharepoint and Onedriv

claims.claim: The roadmap describes the previous configuration as requiring policy tips and email notifications to be enabled together.
claims.quote: As of today, whenever the user wants to enable email notifications the policy tips also need to be enabled and vice versa

claims.claim: An administrator can configure neither policy tips nor email notifications.
claims.quote: 1) None of policy tips or email notification

claims.claim: An administrator can configure only policy tips.
claims.quote: 2) Only policy tips

claims.claim: An administrator can configure only email notifications.
claims.quote: 3) Only Email Notifications

claims.claim: An administrator can configure both email notifications and policy tips.
claims.quote: 4) Both Email Notifications and Policy tips

claims.claim: The reference documents -NotifyUserType with the values NotSet, Email, PolicyTip and Email,PolicyTip.
claims.quote:
The NotifyUserType parameter specifies the type of notification that's used for the rule. Valid values are:
- NotSet
- Email
- PolicyTip
- Email,PolicyTip

claims.claim: Notification type is configured per DLP rule.
claims.quote: The NotifyUserType parameter specifies the type of notification that's used for the rule.

claims.claim: Set-DlpComplianceRule -Identity <rule name or GUID> -NotifyUserType Email,PolicyTip modifies a rule to use both notification types.
claims.quote:
The Identity parameter specifies the DLP rule that you want to modify. You can use any value that uniquely identifies the rule. For example:
- Name
- Distinguished name (DN)
- GUID
- Id
The NotifyUserType parameter specifies the type of notification that's used for the rule.

claims.claim: Set-DlpComplianceRule is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table and prose
claims.claim: The printed Microsoft Purview portal creation route reaches User Notifications in a SharePoint and OneDrive DLP rule.
claims.quote:
Select Custom from both the Categories list and the Regulations list.
On the Define policy settings page, the Create or customize advanced DLP rules option should already be selected.
Set the User Notifications toggle to On.
claims.fix: Use this fuller route in both copies of the table: 'Data loss prevention > Policies > + Create policy > Enterprise applications & devices > Categories: Custom > Regulations: Custom > Assign admin units > Choose where to apply the policy > SharePoint sites > OneDrive accounts > Define policy settings > Create or customize advanced DLP rules > Customize advanced DLP rules > + Create rule > User Notifications'. The category and regulation selections are documented despite the automatic word check; the omitted scope steps and already-selected advanced-rules option are not blockers. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/dlp-create-policy-spo-odb-external.

claims.claim: The creation walkthrough selects Notify users in Office 365 services with a policy tip and then chooses who is notified.
claims.quote: Select Notify users in Office 365 services with a policy tip and then select Notify the user who sent, shared, or last modified the content.

claims.claim: The policy creation and deployment account must belong to one of the role groups listed in the creation guidance.
claims.quote:
The account you use to create and deploy policies must be a member of one of these role groups:
- Compliance administrator
- Compliance data administrator
- Information Protection
- Information Protection Admin
- Security administrator

claims.claim: The listed administrative role groups provide permissions to edit DLP policies.
claims.quote:
Information Protection Admin | Create, edit, and delete DLP policies, sensitivity labels and their policies, and all classifier types.
DLP Compliance Management | View and edit settings and reports for data loss prevention (DLP) policies.
claims.fix: Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-office-365/scc-permissions for the editing-permissions statement; the creation page already cited explicitly states creation and deployment permissions, while the role reference states editing permissions.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: A DLP rule can send email notifications describing a policy conflict to selected people.
claims.quote:
When you create a DLP policy, you can configure the user notifications to:
- Send an email notification to the people you choose that describes the issue.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: SharePoint and OneDrive policy tips can appear as warning icons on documents.
claims.quote: For documents in a OneDrive account or SharePoint site, the policy tip shows as a warning icon that appears on the item.

claims.claim: Notification emails are sent unprotected.
claims.quote: Notification emails are sent unprotected.

claims.claim: A custom notification email body for SharePoint or OneDrive can include %%MatchedConditions%%.
claims.quote:
You can also use the following tokens to help customize the body of the email.
| %%MatchedConditions%% | The conditions that the content matched. Use this token to inform people of possible issues with the content. | Yes | Yes | Yes |

claims.claim: Learn says email notifications trigger only for new content, not edits to existing content.
claims.quote: Only new content triggers an email notification. Editing existing content triggers policy tips, but not email notifications.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Before rollout
claims.claim: Learn says editing existing content triggers policy tips.
claims.quote: Editing existing content triggers policy tips, but not email notifications.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: The DLP policy reference says user overrides require Notify users in Office 365 services with a policy tip to be enabled.
claims.quote: User overrides are enabled only when Notify users in Office 365 services with a policy tip is enabled, so user overrides go hand-in-hand with Notifications and Policy tips.

claims.claim: SharePoint and Exchange overrides are configured in the user notification section.
claims.quote: For Exchange online and SharePoint in Microsoft 365, you configure overrides in the user notification section.

claims.claim: A blocked icon appears on a SharePoint or OneDrive document when a matching rule uses policy tips and blocks access.
claims.quote:
When a document on a OneDrive site or SharePoint site matches a rule in a DLP policy that uses policy tips, special icons appear on the document:
If the rule blocks access to the document, the blocked icon appears.

claims.claim: Email notifications support individual recipients, not groups or distribution lists.
claims.quote: You can send email notifications only to individual recipients, not to groups or distribution lists.

claims.claim: Email recipients can include the content owner, last modifier, site owner or a specific user.
claims.quote: These people can include the owner of the content, the person who last modified the content, the owner of the site where the content is stored, or a specific user.
